definition_en: to operate a vehicle so that it moves, or to force someone or something to act or move

scene: 清晨的公路上薄雾未散，爸爸坐进车里发动了引擎。My father will drive me to school before his first meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 drive 是「开车送、驾驶」（第 1 个义项：操作车辆使其移动）；句意：爸爸会在第一个会议之前开车送我去学校。

senses.title: Operate a vehicle
senses.definition: to control a car, bus, or other vehicle and make it move
senses.definitionCN: 操控汽车、公共汽车等车辆使其行驶
senses.example: She drives the children to school every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上开车送孩子们上学。
senses.why: Driving is the oldest sense: the wheel is held and the vehicle is pushed forward.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶是最早的义项：手握住方向盘，把车辆向前推。

senses.title: Force someone to act
senses.definition: to push a person to do something, often with strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地推动某人做某事，常带强烈情绪
senses.example: Hunger drove the family to leave their village.
senses.exampleCN: 饥饿驱使这家人离开村庄。
senses.why: The image of pushing a vehicle forward grows into pushing a person toward action.
senses.whyCN: 把车辆往前推的意象，长出了把人推向行动的引申义。

senses.title: Power a machine
senses.definition: to provide the energy that makes a machine or system work
senses.definitionCN: 为机器或系统提供使其运转的能量
senses.example: The engine drives the wheels of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机驱动卡车的车轮。
senses.why: A machine, like a car, is moved by a force acting on it, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 机器像车一样被外力推动，所以共用同一个词。

senses.title: Push animals away
senses.definition: to make animals or people move in a direction by force
senses.definitionCN: 用力使动物或人朝某个方向移动
senses.example: The farmer drove the sheep into the pen.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把羊赶进围栏。
senses.why: Herdsmen literally drove cattle along roads long before cars existed.
senses.whyCN: 早在汽车出现之前，牧人就已经在路上驱赶牛群了。

senses.title: Strong energy or desire
senses.definition: a strong inner force that makes a person want to act
senses.definitionCN: 使人想要行动的强烈内在力量
senses.example: Her drive to win impressed the coach.
senses.exampleCN: 她的求胜干劲给教练留下深刻印象。
senses.why: The pushing force inside a machine becomes the pushing force inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 机器内部的推动力，变成了人内心的推动力。

senses.title: A road for vehicles
senses.definition: a short road leading to a house, or a wide street
senses.definitionCN: 通向住宅的短车道，或宽阔的街道
senses.example: A car stopped at the end of the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆车停在长车道尽头。
senses.why: The road built for driving took the verb as its name.
senses.whyCN: 专供行驶的路，便用这个动词命名。

intro.en: Drive is an old Germanic word about pushing things forward, first animals, then vehicles, then machines and minds.
intro.cn: drive 是一个古老的日耳曼词，核心是「把东西向前推」：先是牲畜，后是车辆，再到机器与人心。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic root *driban meant to push or drive forward, used of driving cattle.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根 *driban 意为向前推、驱赶，用于驱赶牲畜。

items.en: Old English drīfan meant to force to move, to urge onward, for both animals and people.
items.cn: 古英语 drīfan 意为迫使移动、催促前行，对象既包括牲畜也包括人。

items.en: In Middle English the word covered forcing people onward and pushing wheeled vehicles.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词既指迫使他人前行，也指推动带轮的车辆。

items.en: With railways and cars, drive settled as the main word for operating a vehicle, then spread to engines and motivation.
items.cn: 随铁路与汽车兴起，drive 成为操作车辆的主要用词，进而扩展到发动机与动机。

items.en: The Latin cognate graidhi, to step forward, is a distant reconstructed relative behind the pushing idea.
items.cn: 拉丁语同源词 graidhi（向前迈步）是「推」这一意象背后较远的重构同源词。

note.en: These words stand near drive in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 drive 相邻。

items.en: Old English drȳge meant dry, free from moisture.

items.en: Old Norse drygr may have influenced the Middle English vowel.

items.en: Middle English dri extended to drought, thirst and plain talk.

items.en: Modern English settled the verb to dry and the dry humour of quiet comedy.

intro.en: During is the present participle of an old verb of lasting, hardened into a preposition.
intro.cn: during 原是一个表示「持续」的古老动词的现在分词，后来固化成介词。

items.en: Old French durer meant to last, from Latin durare.
items.cn: 古法语 durer 意为持续，来自拉丁语 durare。

items.en: Latin durare meant to harden or endure, the root behind durable and duration.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durare 意为变硬、持续，是 durable 与 duration 的词根。

items.en: Middle English kept endure as a verb and used during as its participle, meaning while lasting.
items.cn: 中古英语保留动词 endure，并用 during 作其分词，意为「在持续期间」。

items.en: Gradually during stopped needing a verb and worked alone as a preposition.
items.cn: 渐渐地 during 不再依附动词，独立充当介词。

items.en: Modern English fixed it as the standard preposition for periods of time.
items.cn: 现代英语把它定型为表示时间段的标准介词。

definition_zh: 责任；义务；职责；关税；值日
definition_en: something you must do because it is right or your job, or a tax on goods
core_image: 肩上稳稳放着一件必须扛住的东西
scene: 考试结束后，值日生独自留下擦净整块黑板。It is the monitor's duty to lock the classroom after class.

senses.title: A required task
senses.definition: a task that your job or position requires you to do
senses.definitionCN: 因职务或身份而必须完成的任务
senses.example: It is the monitor's duty to lock the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 锁上教室是班长的职责。
senses.why: The weight is fixed on the shoulder by your role, not by choice.
senses.whyCN: 这份重量由你的角色固定在肩上，而非个人选择。

senses.title: A moral obligation
senses.definition: something a person ought to do because it is right

senses.example: He helped the stranger out of a sense of duty.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于责任感帮助了那位陌生人。

senses.whyCN: 这笔钱同样因规则而必须缴纳，而非出于选择。

senses.title: Being on duty

intro.en: Duty grew from the idea of what is owed, the same root that gives due.

items.en: The phrase each other grew from ech and other into a fixed reciprocal.

items.en: Modern English settled each as the standard single-by-single determiner.
items.cn: 现代英语把 each 定型为标准的逐个限定词。

senses.title: Shaking of the ground
senses.definition: a sudden shaking of the ground caused by the release of strain along a fault
senses.definitionCN: 断层上的应变释放所引起的地面突然震动
senses.example: The earthquake knocked down two walls but left the square intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这场地震震塌了两堵墙，却让广场本身完好无损。
senses.why: earthquake is a plain English compound: earth plus quake, a shaking, so the word names the ground doing what the verb means.
senses.whyCN: earthquake 是朴素的英语复合词：earth「大地」加 quake「震动」，词面就是大地在震。

senses.title: A recorded seismic event
senses.titleCN: 被记录的一次地震事件
senses.definition: a single event entered in a catalogue with a time, location, depth and magnitude
senses.definitionCN: 以时间、位置、深度与震级登记入目录的一次事件
senses.example: The catalogue lists three earthquakes within ten kilometres of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 目录列出该镇十公里范围内的三次地震。
senses.why: once networks record events, earthquake becomes a countable unit of data rather than only an experience.
senses.whyCN: 当台网记录事件之后，earthquake 就不只是人的体验，而成为可计数的数据单位。

senses.title: The main shock of a sequence
senses.definition: the largest event of a sequence, distinguished from the smaller foreshocks and aftershocks
senses.definitionCN: 一次序列中最大的事件，区别于较小的前震与余震
senses.example: The earthquake was followed by forty smaller shocks that night.
senses.exampleCN: 那晚主震之后又发生了四十次较小的震动。
senses.why: a sequence needs a head, so the plain noun came to mean the main shock and the others received prefixed names.
senses.whyCN: 一个序列需要有一个头，因此朴素名词被用来指主震，其余事件则获得带前缀的名称。

senses.title: An induced earthquake
senses.definition: a quake triggered by human activity such as reservoir filling, mining or fluid injection
senses.definitionCN: 由水库蓄水、采矿或流体注入等人类活动触发的地震
senses.example: The injection well caused an earthquake large enough to crack nearby foundations.
senses.exampleCN: 注入井引发了足以震裂附近地基的地震。
senses.why: the mechanism differs but the shaking is the same, so the same noun is kept with an adjective of cause.
senses.whyCN: 机制不同，但震动本身相同，因此保留同一个名词，另加表示成因的形容词。

senses.title: A quake on another world
senses.definition: a seismic event on the Moon, Mars or another solid body
senses.definitionCN: 月球、火星或其他固态天体上的地震事件
senses.example: Instruments left on the Moon recorded an earthquake deep in its crust.
senses.exampleCN: 留在月面的仪器记录到月壳深处的一次地震。
senses.why: the word is extended literally to other bodies, though specialists often prefer moonquake or marsquake.
senses.whyCN: 该词被字面扩展到其他天体，尽管专家往往更爱用 moonquake 或 marsquake。

senses.title: A violent upheaval in society
senses.definition: a sudden, far-reaching change that shakes the established order
senses.definitionCN: 突然而深远、动摇既有秩序的变化
senses.example: The reform was an earthquake in the country's legal tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改革是该国法律传统中的一场地震。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the physical event wholesale: what shakes is no longer ground but an institution.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻整体借用了物理事件：被摇动的不再是地面，而是一套制度。

senses.title: A shock to a market or organization
senses.titleCN: 对市场或组织的巨大冲击
senses.definition: a disruptive shock that forces rapid restructuring in business or finance
senses.definitionCN: 迫使商业或金融迅速重组的颠覆性冲击
senses.example: The collapse of the carrier was an earthquake for regional airports.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司的倒闭对地区机场是一场地震。
senses.why: economic writing uses the same metaphor because markets, like ground, can lose their bearings.
senses.whyCN: 经济写作使用同一比喻，因为市场与地面一样会失去依托。

senses.title: A disaster category
senses.titleCN: 灾害与保险中的地震类别
senses.definition: a class of natural disaster used in relief planning, insurance and building codes
senses.definitionCN: 用于救援规划、保险与建筑规范的一类自然灾害
senses.example: The policy covers earthquake but not flooding.
senses.exampleCN: 该保单承保地震，但不承保洪水。
senses.why: institutions need to sort hazards into named categories, and the everyday word becomes an administrative one.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要把危险归入有名字的类别，于是日常词变成了行政术语。

intro.en: Earthquake is a native English compound of earth, from Old English eorþe, and quake, from Old English cwacian, to tremble. It is recorded in English from the late thirteenth century and has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: earthquake 是英语本族复合词：earth 来自古英语 eorþe，quake 来自古英语 cwacian「颤抖」。英语文献中自 13 世纪后期即有记录，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Eorþe meant the ground, soil or the world; it survives as earth in modern English and supplies the first element of the compound.
items.cn: eorþe 指大地、土壤或世界；它在现代英语中存为 earth，并构成这个复合词的前一部分。

items.en: Cwacian meant to tremble or shake; its noun quake first meant a trembling of the body before it was applied to the ground.
items.cn: cwacian 意为颤抖或摇动；其名词 quake 最初指身体的发抖，后来才用于地面。

items.en: English joined the two words in the late thirteenth century, at first in forms such as eorþe-cwace, to name the ground shaking.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪后期把两个词拼合，早期形式如 eorþe-cwace，用来指地面震动。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word entered scientific writing, and later catalogues made each event a countable unit.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，该词进入科学写作；后来的地震目录把每次事件变成可计数的单位。

items.en: Modern usage extends earthquake figuratively to political, social and economic shocks that rearrange the ground under an institution.
items.cn: 现代用法把 earthquake 比喻扩展到政治、社会与经济冲击，它们重新排布制度脚下的地面。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest recorded spelling varies between eorþe-cwace and earthquake, and the exact first citation date is given only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：最早的拼写形式在 eorþe-cwace 与 earthquake 之间不同，确切的最早书证年代只能给约数。

note.en: Group one holds the English words built from the same two elements; group two holds terms for shaking events and for upheavals.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个成分构成的英语词；第二组是表示震动事件与剧变的词。

entries.definition: The second element used alone: a verb meaning to tremble, and an informal noun for an earthquake.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用的后一成分：动词指颤抖，口语名词指地震。

entries.definition: Built on earth plus shake rather than quake, and now mostly figurative for overwhelmingly important.
entries.definitionCN: 由 earth 加 shake 而非 quake 构成，如今多作比喻指「极其重大」。

entries.definition: Earthquake plus proof in the sense of resistant: built so as not to fail in a quake.
entries.definitionCN: earthquake 加 proof（意为「抗」）：建造得能在震中不失效。

entries.definition: Earthquake plus prone: describing a region likely to experience quakes.
entries.definitionCN: earthquake 加 prone：描述容易发生地震的地区。

entries.definition: A minor earthquake or a continuous shaking; it is usually weaker than an earthquake and can also mean a bodily shake.
entries.definitionCN: 小地震或持续的轻微震动；通常比 earthquake 弱，也可指身体颤抖。

entries.definition: A sudden violent jolt, whether seismic, electrical or emotional; it names the impact rather than the geological event.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的猛烈冲击，可以是地震的、电的或情绪的；指冲击而非地质事件。

entries.definition: A chiefly American Spanish-derived term for an earthquake, common in news from seismic regions.
entries.definitionCN: 主要在美国使用、源自西班牙语的「地震」说法，常见于地震区新闻。

entries.definition: A violent or major change in society or a person's life; unlike earthquake it has no literal geological use.
entries.definitionCN: 社会或个人生活中的剧烈重大变化；与 earthquake 不同，它没有字面地质用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: earth + quake: the ground doing the trembling.
normal.cn: earth + quake：大地在发抖。

normal.en: The family runs earthquake, earthquakes, quake, earthquake-proof, earthquake-resistant, earthquake-prone.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 earthquake、earthquakes、quake、earthquake-proof、earthquake-resistant、earthquake-prone。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: earthquake damage, earthquake zone, earthquake drill, earthquake insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地震破坏、地震区、地震演练、地震保险。

normal.en: News usage: a strong earthquake struck at dawn; the magnitude was revised upward.
normal.cn: 新闻用法：一场强震在黎明袭击；震级被上调。

normal.en: The -quake element also appears in moonquake and marsquake for other bodies.
normal.cn: -quake 成分也出现在指其他天体的 moonquake 与 marsquake 中。

abstract.en: Picture a boardroom table splitting down the middle during a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一张董事会议桌在投票时从中间裂开。

abstract.en: Picture a price list whose numbers all change while the shopkeeper is still writing.
abstract.cn: 想象店主还在写价目表，上面的数字就全变了。

abstract.en: Picture a constitution whose paragraphs slide past one another like fault blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一部宪法的条款像断块一样互相错动。

examples.en: The earthquake destroyed the old bridge and cut the only road.
examples.cn: 地震摧毁了那座旧桥，切断了唯一的道路。

examples.en: Engineers design hospitals to remain open after a major earthquake.
examples.cn: 工程师把医院设计成在大地震后仍能运转。

examples.en: The discovery of the letters was an earthquake in the study of the period.
examples.cn: 这批信件的发现使该时期的研究发生了地震般的震荡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「earth（大地）+ quake（抖）」——大地发抖 → 地震

root: 英语本族复合词：古英语 eorþe「大地」+ cwacian「颤抖」的名词 quake；无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shaking from ground to catalogue: the physical event, the recorded event, the main shock, the human-caused and off-world variants, then society, markets and finally the administrative category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一场震动从地面走进目录：物理事件、被记录的事件、主震、人为与地外变体，再到社会、市场，最后成为行政类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paving stones shifted out of line and a crack opening down a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺地砖石错位，墙体从上到下裂开。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL EVENT: the ground moves because strain is released.
branches.cn: 物理事件：应变释放，地面因此移动。

branches.en: THE CATALOGUE: an event becomes a row of data, with a head and smaller followers.
branches.cn: 目录：事件变成一行数据，有头部，也有较小的跟随者。

branches.en: CHANGED CAUSE AND PLACE: humans can trigger it, and other worlds can host it.
branches.cn: 成因与场所的变换：人类可以触发它，别的世界也可以承载它。

branches.en: METAPHOR: institutions and markets are shaken until their old alignments fail.
branches.cn: 比喻：制度与市场被摇到旧有对齐失效。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATIVE BOX: the event becomes a category that policies and codes refer to.
branches.cn: 行政归类：事件变成一个保单与规范可以引用的类别。

intro.en: Earthquake is a native compound of two free morphemes, and its second element also lives alone as a verb and an informal noun.
intro.cn: earthquake 是由两个自由语素构成的本族复合词，其第二成分也能独立作动词与口语名词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin elements are involved: both halves are inherited Germanic words, though Latin terra and quatere are only semantic parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 不涉及拉丁成分：两半都是继承的日耳曼语词；拉丁 terra 与 quatere 只是语义上的平行词，并非来源。

items.exampleCN: earth 提供被摇动的对象。

definition_zh: 容易地；轻松地；很可能；无疑地
definition_en: without difficulty or effort, or very likely and without doubt
core_image: 一片羽毛轻轻松手便滑落
scene: 外婆坐在门口，把毛线针在指间绕得不费力气。My grandmother easily finishes one sock every evening.

senses.title: Without difficulty
senses.definition: in a way that needs little effort or causes no trouble
senses.definitionCN: 以几乎不需要力气或不引起麻烦的方式
senses.example: My grandmother easily finishes one sock every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆每晚都能轻松织完一只袜子。
senses.why: The action runs smooth because nothing blocks it.
senses.whyCN: 动作顺畅进行，因为没有任何阻碍。

senses.title: Very likely
senses.definition: used to say that something is quite possible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事很有可能发生
senses.example: The fire could easily spread in dry weather.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥天气里火很容易蔓延。
senses.why: When nothing blocks a thing, it is free to happen.
senses.whyCN: 当没有任何东西阻挡时，事情就容易成真。

senses.title: Without doubt
senses.definition: used to stress that a claim is certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 强调某种说法毫无疑问
senses.example: She is easily the strongest player in the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是俱乐部里最强的棋手。
senses.why: No effort needed to judge: the answer lies open.
senses.whyCN: 判断毫不费力：答案一目了然。

intro.en: Easily is easy plus ly, and easy itself comes from a Latin word for room and comfort.
intro.cn: easily 是 easy 加 ly，而 easy 源自一个表示「空间、安逸」的拉丁词。

items.en: Latin aptus meant fitted, suited; its Old French descendant aisie meant at ease.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aptus 意为合适的；其古法语后裔 aisie 意为安适的。

items.en: Old French aisie, from aise, ease, described a person without trouble.
items.cn: 古法语 aisie（源自 aise，安逸）形容没有烦恼的人。

items.en: The noun aise meant comfort and room to live.
items.cn: 名词 aise 意为舒适与生活的余地。

items.en: Middle English ese, easy came in as comfort and freedom from pain.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ese、easy 带着舒适与免于痛苦之义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English built easily as the natural adverb of easy.
items.cn: 现代英语把 easily 定为 easy 的自然副词形式。

note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 easily 相邻。

examples.en: The little boy easily lifted the empty box.

examples.en: Glass items break easily when they are packed badly.

examples.en: He is easily the kindest person in our class.

definition_zh: 东；东方；向东；东方的
definition_en: the direction where the sun rises, or the part of a country or world that lies that way
core_image: 清晨太阳从地平线升起的那一边
scene: 海边的清晨，渔民背对着朝阳收网归来。The fishing boats sailed east along the calm coast.

senses.title: The direction of sunrise
senses.definition: the point of the horizon where the sun rises
senses.definitionCN: 地平线上太阳升起的方位
senses.example: The temple gate faces east to greet the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 寺庙大门朝东，迎接日出。
senses.why: The oldest anchor is the daily sunrise itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的锚点就是每日的日出。

senses.title: Movement or position toward east
senses.definition: moving or lying in the east direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝东的方向移动或位于东方

senses.exampleCN: 渔船沿着海岸向东航行。

senses.whyCN: 方位变成一条可走的路径。

senses.title: The eastern part of a region
senses.definition: the part of a country, continent, or world that lies toward the east

senses.example: Rain is coming from the east of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 雨正从该省东部过来。
senses.why: The small direction grows into a wide human region.
senses.whyCN: 小小的方位长成广阔的人文地域。

intro.en: East is a Germanic sky word, tied to the brightness of dawn.
intro.cn: east 是一个日耳曼的天空词，与黎明的光亮相连。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *austam meant the direction of dawn, related to a word for shine.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *austam 意为黎明的方向，与表示「闪耀」的词相关。

items.en: Old English ēast named both sunrise and the eastern lands.
items.cn: 古英语 ēast 既指日出之方，也指东方之地。

items.en: Old Norse austr kept the same dawn direction in Viking sailing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 austr 在维京航海中保留同一黎明方位。

items.en: Middle English used east for maps, trade winds and eastern peoples.
items.cn: 中古英语把 east 用于地图、信风与东方民族。

items.en: Modern English built eastern, eastward and East Asia.
items.cn: 现代英语构出 eastern、eastward 与 East Asia 等。

note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 east 相邻。

definition_zh: 容易的；不费力的；舒适的；安逸的；随和的
definition_en: not difficult, needing little effort, or comfortable and relaxed
core_image: 一只手不用劲就推开了没上锁的门
scene: 体育课后，同学们瘫坐在草坪上享受难得的空闲。The last question on the test was easy for everyone.

derivatives.zh: easy 加 ly 构成，义为「容易地」
同源名词，义为「容易；安逸」

senses.title: Not difficult
senses.definition: needing little effort or skill to do or understand
senses.definitionCN: 做起来或理解起来不需要多少力气或技巧
senses.example: The last question on the test was easy for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 试卷最后一题对每个人都很容易。
senses.why: The door opens because nothing is holding it shut.
senses.whyCN: 门之所以好开，是因为没有任何东西锁住它。

senses.title: Comfortable and relaxed
senses.definition: free from pain, worry, or hard work
senses.definitionCN: 没有疼痛、担忧或辛苦
senses.example: They live an easy life by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边过着安逸的生活。
senses.why: The roominess of a comfortable life is the same freedom from blocks.
senses.whyCN: 安逸生活的从容，正是同一种没有阻碍的自由。

senses.title: Relaxed in manner
senses.definition: friendly and not easily worried or offended
senses.definitionCN: 友好而不易焦虑或生气的
senses.example: Our new teacher is easy to talk to.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新老师和蔼健谈。
senses.why: A person without inner blocks is pleasant to meet.
senses.whyCN: 内心没有阻碍的人让人乐于亲近。

intro.en: Easy comes from a Latin word for fitted, arriving through French words for comfort.
intro.cn: easy 来自拉丁语「合适的」一词，经法语「安逸」一路传入。

items.en: Latin aptus meant fitted, suited, well placed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aptus 意为合适的、恰当的。

items.en: Old French aisie, at ease, described a person free of trouble.
items.cn: 古法语 aisie（安适的）形容没有烦恼的人。

items.en: The noun aise meant comfort and breathing room.
items.cn: 名词 aise 意为舒适与从容的余地。

items.en: Middle English ese and easy meant comfort and freedom from pain.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ese 与 easy 表示舒适与免于痛苦。

items.en: Modern English extended easy to tasks, lives and personalities.
items.cn: 现代英语把 easy 扩展到任务、生活与性格。

note.en: These words stand near easy in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 easy 相邻。

definition_zh: 吃；进食；侵蚀；消耗
definition_en: to put food in the mouth and swallow it, or to wear something away gradually
core_image: 一口一口把食物送进嘴里
scene: 放学路上，烤红薯的香气从街角飘来。The children stopped to eat sweet roasted potatoes on the way home.
sceneCN: 这里 eat 是「吃」（第 1 个义项：把食物放入口中咽下）；句意：孩子们在放学路上停下来吃香甜的烤红薯。

derivatives.zh: eat 加表示者的后缀 er 构成，义为「食者」
同源拉丁词根的形容词，义为「可食用的」

senses.title: Chew and swallow food
senses.definition: to put food in the mouth, chew it, and swallow it
senses.definitionCN: 把食物放入口中咀嚼并咽下
senses.example: The children stopped to eat roasted potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们停下来吃烤红薯。
senses.why: The body takes in fuel a bite at a time.
senses.whyCN: 身体一口一口地摄入燃料。

senses.title: Have a meal regularly
senses.definition: to have a meal at a stated time or place
senses.definitionCN: 在固定时间或地点用餐
senses.example: We eat at six every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每天傍晚六点吃饭。
senses.why: One act of eating becomes the standing habit of meals.
senses.whyCN: 一次进食的动作成为固定的用餐习惯。

senses.title: Wear away gradually
senses.definition: to destroy or consume something slowly, as acid or rust does
senses.definitionCN: 像酸或锈那样缓慢地破坏或消耗某物
senses.example: Salt water eats away the iron hull.
senses.exampleCN: 海水慢慢侵蚀铁制船体。
senses.why: What consumes food consumes metal the same way, slowly and steadily.
senses.whyCN: 吞噬食物的东西同样缓慢而稳定地吞噬金属。

intro.en: Eat is one of the oldest words in English, straight from the common Indo-European root of biting.
intro.cn: eat 是英语最古老的词之一，直接来自印欧语「咬食」的共同词根。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *etan meant to eat, from the Indo-European root *ed-, to bite.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *etan 意为吃，来自印欧词根 *ed-（咬食）。

items.en: Old English etan meant to eat and consume.
items.cn: 古英语 etan 意为吃、消耗。

items.en: The same root appears in Latin edere, which gives edible and oblige relations.
items.cn: 同一词根也见于拉丁语 edere，派生出 edible 等词。

items.en: Old English also used the word of gnawing and wasting, planting the erosion sense.
items.cn: 古英语也用该词表示啃咬与消耗，埋下侵蚀义的种子。

items.en: Modern English added eat out, eat up and eat away.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 eat out、eat up 与 eat away 等短语。

note.en: These words stand near eat in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 eat 相邻。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；训练；向公众普及知识
definition_en: to teach, train or develop someone's knowledge, skill and judgment
core_image: 一个人牵着孩子的手，从黑暗的屋子一步步走到门口，门外的光是孩子自己看见的
scene: 博物馆把库房里的标本搬到走廊，让孩子可以伸手触摸并提问。The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
sceneCN: 这里 educate 指向公众传授知识、培养理解（第 3 个义项：向公众普及）；句意为博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；训练（可指学校教育，也可指培养判断力）
向公众普及；告知（常与 public、consumers 等搭配）

derivatives.zh: 教育；教育学（由 educate 加表示「动作」的后缀构成，转指培养的过程与制度）
教育工作者（由 educate 加表示「执行者」的后缀构成，转指以教育为职业的人）
教育的；有教育意义的（由 education 加表示「属于」的后缀构成）
有教育作用的（由 educate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指能带来教益）
引出；使显现（由拉丁 educere「引出」进入英语，与 educate 同源但义不同）

senses.title: To teach in school
senses.definition: to provide formal instruction, usually in a school or college
senses.definitionCN: 通常在学校或学院提供正式教学
senses.example: The school educates children from six to sixteen.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校教育六岁到十六岁的孩子。
senses.why: This is the everyday school sense: an institution and a curriculum carry the act.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的学校义：机构与课程承载这一动作。

senses.title: To bring up and nurture
senses.definition: to care for a person's growth and character over time, not only their knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料一个人的成长与品格，而不只是知识
senses.example: Her grandmother educated her in patience as much as in letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母教她认字，也教她耐心。
senses.why: The Latin verb began with rearing, and this older sense survives whenever the object is a whole person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词最初指养育，只要宾语是完整的人，这层古老义就仍在。

senses.title: To inform the public
senses.definition: to help a broad audience understand an issue, often through campaigns, exhibits or media
senses.definitionCN: 通过宣传活动、展览或媒体帮助广泛受众理解某一议题
senses.example: The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。
senses.why: The object widens from a pupil to the public, and the verb becomes a form of public communication.
senses.whyCN: 宾语从学生扩到公众，这个动词就变成一种公共传播。

senses.title: To train in a skill
senses.definition: to develop practical ability through instruction and practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过指导与练习发展实际能力
senses.example: The course educates new staff in safe handling of chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程训练新员工安全处理化学品。
senses.why: Skill training narrows the verb from general development to a demonstrable competence.
senses.whyCN: 技能训练把这个动词从一般发展收窄到可演示的能力。

senses.title: To cultivate taste or judgment
senses.definition: to refine someone's ability to notice, compare and decide
senses.definitionCN: 提升某人察觉、比较与判断的能力
senses.example: Travel educated his eye for architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行培养了他对建筑的眼光。
senses.why: The verb can take an inner faculty as its object, so education becomes the training of perception.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以拿内在能力作宾语，教育于是成为感知的训练。

senses.title: To inform consumers
senses.definition: to give buyers information so that they can choose or use a product responsibly
senses.definitionCN: 向买家提供信息，使其能负责地选择或使用产品
senses.example: The label educates consumers about where the beans were grown.
senses.exampleCN: 标签告知消费者咖啡豆的产地。
senses.why: Business uses the word for disclosure: the seller teaches, though often within a marketing frame.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词表示信息披露：卖方在教，尽管常在营销框架内。

senses.title: To educate oneself
senses.definition: to pursue knowledge or skill without being taught by an institution
senses.definitionCN: 不经机构教学而自行追求知识或技能
senses.example: He educated himself in law while working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他上夜班时自学法律。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the verb inward: the same person is both teacher and learner.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把这个动词转向内部：同一个人既是教师也是学习者。

senses.title: Abstract: to lead out of ignorance
senses.definition: to help someone move from not knowing to knowing, whatever the method
senses.definitionCN: 以任何方式帮助某人从不知走向知
senses.example: A single good question can educate more than a long lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题有时比一堂长讲座更能教育人。
senses.why: At its most abstract the verb names the movement of a mind, not a classroom or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个动词命名心智的移动，而非教室或大纲。

intro.en: Educate comes from Latin educare 'to bring up, rear', closely related to educere 'to lead out' (ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead'). It entered English in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: educate 来自拉丁 educare「养育、培养」，与 educere「引出」关系密切，后者由表示「向外」的成分加 ducere「引导」构成。它在十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. Its family includes conduct, introduce, reduce and produce.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」。其词族包括 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 produce。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ducere gave educere 'to lead out'. The image is drawing a person out of ignorance rather than filling them.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的成分加 ducere 构成 educere「引出」。意象是把人从无知中拉出来，而非往里面填东西。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is a related verb, and Latin writers already used it alongside educere.
items.cn: educare 意为「养育、抚养、培养」。它是一个相关动词，拉丁作家已把它与 educere 并用。

items.en: English educate appeared in the fifteenth century, first meaning to rear or bring up, then to instruct formally.
items.cn: 英语 educate 在十五世纪出现，最初指养育，后来指正式教导。

items.en: The pair educare and educere are often confused: one stresses nurture, the other the movement out. Both images survive in the English word.
items.cn: educare 与 educere 这对动词常被混淆：一个强调养育，一个强调向外移动。两种意象都留在英语词里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and relationship): the exact first English use is not recorded, and the precise relation between educare and educere is disputed among etymologists.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与关系）：英语最早用例没有精确记录；educare 与 educere 的确切关系在词源学家之间有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the verb from same-root relatives and from a look-alike of a different root; group two holds the everyday verbs for teaching.
note.cn: 第一组把这个动词与同根亲属词、以及一个异源形近词分开；第二组是表示教导的日常动词。

entries.definition: To draw out something hidden or potential; educate develops a person, while educe extracts what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 把隐藏或潜在之物引出；educate 发展一个人，educe 则提取已经存在之物。

entries.definition: The process or system; the verb names the act that the noun describes.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或制度；动词命名名词所描述的动作。

entries.definition: From in- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a role or knowledge. It shares the leading root but adds entry.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「进入」的成分加 ducere 构成：把某人引入一个角色或知识。它与「引导」同根，却加上「进入」。

entries.definition: From Latin dicare 'to declare', not ducere. It means to devote or inscribe, with no teaching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dicare「宣告」，并非 ducere；意为奉献或题献，没有教学义。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for helping someone learn; educate is more formal and often implies a longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某人学习的日常动词；educate 更正式，常含较长的过程。

entries.definition: To give explicit directions or lessons; it stresses transmission, while educate can stress development.
entries.definitionCN: 给出明确指令或课程；它强调传递，而 educate 可强调发展。

entries.definition: To develop a specific skill through repeated practice; educate is broader and includes judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复练习发展特定技能；educate 更宽，包含判断力。

entries.definition: To educate in an institution, or to train someone firmly; it is narrower and often more severe in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 在机构中教育，或严格训练某人；它更窄，语气常更严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ducere means lead, so educate is to lead someone out of not knowing.
normal.cn: ducere 意为引导，所以 educate 是把人从不知中引出来。

normal.en: The two Latin verbs split the work: one rears, the other leads out, and English keeps both images.
normal.cn: 两个拉丁动词分工：一个养育，一个引出，英语保留两种意象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the objects: educate children, educate the public, educate consumers.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示宾语：教育孩子、向公众普及、教育消费者。

normal.en: The reflexive form educates yourself turns the teacher and learner into one person.
normal.cn: 反身形式 educate yourself 把教师与学习者合成一个人。

normal.en: Educe is the bare 'draw out' cousin, with no school attached.
normal.cn: educe 是不带学校的「引出」近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a locked cabinet slowly opened, its contents already inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个上锁的柜子被慢慢打开，里面的东西本来就在。

abstract.cn: 想象一个问题让整间屋子先静下来，然后开口。

examples.en: The campaign set out to educate voters about the new ballot rules.
examples.cn: 这场运动旨在向选民普及新的投票规则。

examples.en: She was educated at a small school where every class had two teachers.
examples.cn: 她在一所小规模学校受教育，每个班有两名教师。

examples.en: Travel educated his eye for colour long before he studied painting.
examples.cn: 早在他学画之前，旅行就培养了他对颜色的眼光。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with school instruction, then move to rearing, public information, skill training, taste, consumer disclosure, self-teaching and finally any movement of a mind out of ignorance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学校教学出发，转到养育、公共普及、技能训练、品味、消费者告知、自学，最后是任何把心智引离无知的移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leads a child out of a dark room toward a door of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着孩子，从黑暗的屋子走向一扇有光的门。

branches.en: FORMAL AND PRACTICAL: school instruction, then training in a demonstrable skill.
branches.cn: 正式与实践：先是学校教学，再是可演示的技能训练。

branches.en: GROWTH INSIDE A PERSON: rearing of character, then cultivation of taste and judgment.
branches.cn: 一个人内部的成长：品格的养育，再是品味与判断的培养。

branches.en: OUTWARD INFORMATION: the public is informed, and buyers are told what they need to know.
branches.cn: 向外的信息：公众被告知，买家被告知所需之事。

branches.en: TEACHER AND LEARNER AS ONE: self-education turns the verb inward.
branches.cn: 师生合一：自我教育把这个动词转向内部。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT ITSELF: the widest reading names a mind leaving ignorance.
branches.cn: 移动本身：最宽的读法命名心智离开无知。

intro.en: Educate is a Latin verb of rearing and leading, and English draws a whole school vocabulary from its two related stems.
intro.cn: educate 是一个表示养育与引导的拉丁动词，英语从它两个相关词干取出一整套学校语汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct and introduce; educare gives educate, education, educator and educative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct 与 introduce；educare 衍生 educate、education、educator 与 educative。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；教育学；（尤指）学校教育体系
definition_en: the process of teaching and learning, especially in schools, and the organized system that carries it out
core_image: 午后教室里的黑板、成排课桌与摊开的课本，窗台上摆着一只装满粉笔的旧铁盒
scene: 乡村学校的教室里，黑板擦得发亮，课桌排成几行，课本摊在桌面上。Public education gave every child in the valley a seat and a teacher.
sceneCN: 这里指「教与学的过程，尤指学校中的教育」（第 1 个义项：传授与习得知识的过程）；句意为公共教育让山谷里的每个孩子都有了座位和老师。可辨识物件：黑板、课桌、课本、粉笔盒。

senses.title: The process of teaching and learning
senses.definition: the activity through which knowledge, skills and habits are passed from one person to another
senses.definitionCN: 知识、技能与习惯在人与人之间传递的活动
senses.example: Good education begins with questions rather than answers.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教育从提问而不是从答案开始。
senses.why: the noun came from a verb meaning to bring up and rear, so its core is the whole act of raising someone's mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自表「养育、培养」的动词，其核心是把人的心智养成的整个动作。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized network of schools, teachers, curricula and funding that a state or community maintains
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社区维持的学校、教师、课程与经费的组织网络
senses.example: Rural education improved after the new schools opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校开办之后，乡村教育得到改善。
senses.why: once schooling became a public service, the word shifted from the act to the machine that delivers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦学校教育成为公共服务，这个词就从动作转向提供它的那台机器。

senses.title: A person's upbringing and formation
senses.titleCN: 一个人的教养与成长背景
senses.definition: the whole formation of a person's character and taste, including what happens outside school
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格与品味所受的整体养成，包括校门之外的部分
senses.example: Her education at home was stricter than anything the school imposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家所受的教养比学校的一切要求都更严格。
senses.why: the older sense of rearing survives in phrases about a person's background rather than a system.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「养育」义保留在谈论个人背景的短语里，而不指体系。

senses.title: The academic field of study
senses.definition: the discipline that studies how people learn and how teaching should be organized
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习、教学应如何组织的学科
senses.example: She holds a doctorate in education from a state university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所州立大学取得教育学博士学位。
senses.why: a field of study takes the name of its object, which is why the discipline is simply called education.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科常以其研究对象命名，因此这门学科直接就叫「教育」。

senses.title: A level or stage of schooling
senses.titleCN: 某一阶段或层级的教育
senses.definition: a named stage such as primary, secondary or higher education
senses.definitionCN: 初等、中等或高等教育等具名阶段
senses.example: Fewer girls than boys continued into secondary education.
senses.exampleCN: 继续升入中等教育的女孩少于男孩。
senses.why: the single word covers each named stage, because a stage is only a portion of the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖每一个具名阶段，因为一个阶段只是整个过程中的一段。

senses.title: A public information campaign
senses.titleCN: 面向公众的宣传教育活动
senses.definition: an organized effort to teach the public about health, safety or civic matters
senses.definitionCN: 就健康、安全或公共事务向公众进行的有组织教育
senses.example: The clinic ran a road safety education week.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所办了一周的道路安全教育。
senses.why: the same word covers teaching that has no classroom, because the aim is still to change behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖没有教室的教学，因为目的仍是改变行为。

senses.title: The teaching profession and its work
senses.definition: the occupation of teachers and the professional work they do
senses.definitionCN: 教师的职业及其专业工作
senses.example: She entered education after ten years in engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工程界工作十年后进入教育行业。
senses.why: the activity became an industry with careers, so the word also names the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动成为一个有职业路径的行业，因此这个词也指行业本身。

senses.title: The result: a cultivated mind
senses.titleCN: 教育的结果：被培养出的心智
senses.definition: the knowledge and judgement a person finally possesses as a result of learning
senses.definitionCN: 一个人因学习而最终拥有的知识与判断力
senses.example: His education showed in the way he listened before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的教养体现在他先听后说的方式上。
senses.why: the word can name either the journey or what the traveller carries at the end.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指旅程，也可指旅人最终带着的东西。

intro.en: Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'to bring up, rear'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 educatio「养育、培养」，其动词为 educare「抚养、培育」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is generally connected with the idea of drawing out a person's capacities, though the exact pre-Latin shape is not established.
items.cn: educare 意为「抚养、培育、养育」，一般认为与「把人身上的能力引发出来」这一观念相关，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态未获证明。

items.en: Educere, ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead', meant 'to lead out'. The famous notion of education as leading a mind out rests on this second verb.
items.cn: educere 由 ex-「向外」加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引出」。把教育理解为「把心智引出来」的著名说法，依据的正是这第二个动词。

items.en: Educatio named the rearing and training of a child. English took the noun through French with the same meaning.
items.cn: educatio 指对儿童的抚养与训练，英语经法语借入时保留了同一含义。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word increasingly meant formal instruction in schools rather than upbringing at home.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词越来越多地指学校里的正式教学，而非家庭中的养育。

items.en: In the twentieth century education also became the name of the academic discipline that studies teaching and learning.
items.cn: 二十世纪，「教育」又成为研究教与学的学科的正式名称。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the older verb meant 'nourish' or 'lead out' cannot be settled for the earliest layer, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to lead' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早一层究竟取「养育」还是「引出」，无法定论；有人把它与表「引导」的词根相连，那只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name learning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词衍生、极易混淆的词形；第二组是表示学习的近义词。

entries.definition: To teach or bring up someone; the noun education names the whole activity or system, not a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指教育或培养某人；名词则指整个活动或体系，而非单个动作。

entries.definition: Meaning 'relating to education' or 'instructive', as in an educational visit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与教育有关的」或「有教育意义的」，如一次有教育意义的参观。

entries.definition: Describes a person who has received education; it is a state, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述受过教育的人，是一种状态，而非体系。

entries.definition: A teacher or someone who works in education; the ending marks the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指教师或教育工作者，词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: The formal instruction actually received in schools; it is the measurable part of education.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学校实际受到的正式教学，是教育中可测量的部分。

entries.definition: Practice aimed at a particular skill; it is narrower and usually has a task in view.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某项技能的练习，范围更窄，通常有具体任务。

entries.definition: The knowledge or skill acquired; it names the result rather than the organized giving.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得的知识或技能，说的是结果而非有组织的传授。

entries.definition: Deliberate teaching of content, often in steps; it is a method within education.
entries.definitionCN: 指有步骤地教授内容，是教育之内的种方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs educate, educated, educational, educator, educative.
normal.cn: 同族包括「教育」「受过教育的」「教育的」「教育者」「有教育作用的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: primary, secondary and higher education.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：初等、中等与高等教育。

normal.en: One verb has two readings, nourish and lead out, and both survive in how people talk about teaching.
normal.cn: 同一个动词有「养育」与「引出」两种读法，两种都留在人们谈论教学的方式里。

normal.en: The same noun serves the activity, the system and the discipline.
normal.cn: 同一个名词兼指活动、体系与学科。

normal.en: A classroom with a board, desks and books is the easiest picture to hold.
normal.cn: 有黑板、课桌与书本的教室是最容易抓住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp being lit rather than a bucket being filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被点亮，而不是一只桶被灌满。

abstract.en: Picture a seed given soil, water and time, then growing on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子得到土、水与时间，然后自行生长。

abstract.en: Picture a path with several gates, each opened by a different stage of study.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有几道门的路径，每道门由不同的学习阶段打开。

examples.en: Education is the surest route out of poverty for a whole village.
examples.cn: 对一个村庄来说，教育是摆脱贫困最可靠的路。

examples.en: The ministry spends a third of its budget on basic education.
examples.cn: 该部把三分之一的预算投入基础教育。

examples.en: Her education taught her to read a contract before signing it.
examples.cn: 她所受的教育让她在签字前先读懂合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丢开心」——把不懂的东西一点点丢掉，心就开了，这就是教育。

root: 拉丁 educare「抚养、培育」构成 educatio「养育、训练」；一般认为它与表「引出」的 educere 相关，但「引出说」属后世解释，最早一层含义不能定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person is brought up, and that bringing-up is then organized into schools, stages, a profession and a discipline, until it finally names what the person carries away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个人被养成人，这种养成随后被组织成学校、阶段、职业与学科，最后用来指那个人带走的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp lit in a room rather than a bucket filled from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋里被点亮的一盏灯，而不是从外面灌满的一只桶。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS FRUIT: teaching is both the journey and the judgement carried home.
branches.cn: 动作与果实：教学既是旅程，也是带回家的判断力。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE TRADE: a system of schools needs a profession to run it.
branches.cn: 机器与行业：学校体系需要一支职业队伍来运转。

branches.en: BEFORE AND BEYOND SCHOOL: character is formed at home as much as in class.
branches.cn: 校门内外：性格在家里形成，不比在课堂上少。

branches.en: ORGANIZED KNOWLEDGE: a discipline studies education, while stages divide it.
branches.cn: 被组织起来的知识：一门学科研究教育，而阶段把教育分段。

branches.en: WITHOUT A CLASSROOM: campaigns teach the public where no desk exists.
branches.cn: 没有教室：宣传活动在无课桌处教育公众。

intro.en: The word is a Latin action noun whose verb also builds a compact English family, so it can be read from the verb outward.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其动词在英语里也构成一个紧凑词族，因此可从动词向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin educare 'to rear' and educere 'to lead out' share the element ducere 'to lead'; educatio is the action noun built on the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 educare「养育」与 educere「引出」共享表「引导」的成分；educatio 是在前一个动词上构成的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix turns leading into a movement out of something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「引导」变成「从某处向外」的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a guide walking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「引路者走在前面」的画面。

items.example: The verb names the whole work of raising a child.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指抚养孩子的全部工作。

items.example: They educate their children at home until six.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在六岁前由他们在家教育。

items.meaning: the act, system or result of teaching
items.example: Education changes what a family can imagine.
items.exampleCN: 教育改变一个家庭所能想象的东西。

items.example: The museum runs educational programs for schools.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆为学校开设教育项目。

items.example: The educator trained new teachers in the district.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育工作者在本区培训新教师。

items.example: Failure can be educative if it is examined.
items.exampleCN: 失败若被审视，也能起教育作用。
